Hold-down type and base plate thickness

LocationAll columns SC1, SC2, SC3
Drawing ref.S04.12 Typical Base Plate and Hold Down Bolt Details; S00.03 note S8
Question

S04.12 says 'Braced columns or mullions to be hold down bolt (chemical or post fix anchors not permitted)', but no drawing says which columns are braced. The typical details default to 4M20 H.V.U chemical anchors.

Base plate thickness is also given three ways: 20 (note S8; SHS detail for 150/200 SHS), 12 (100 SHS) and 10 ('ALT SHS', 100 SHS).

Proposal A (our model)
All columns on cast-in 4-M24 4.6/S hold-down bolts. Base plates 20 thick for SC1 (150 SHS) and SC2 (200 SHS), 12 thick for SC3 (100 SHS); plate = column + 180 square (bolts 45 from column face).
Proposal B
Cast-in hold-down bolts only at SC2 (grid 08, carrying the trusses); SC1 and SC3 mezzanine columns on 4M20 H.V.U chemical anchors. Plate thicknesses as A.
Please confirm A or B, and the base plate thicknesses.

TR1 transport splices, apex joint, splice welds and piece heights

LocationTruss TR1 on grid 07, grids A to F (27.4 m)
Drawing ref.S04.03 section 7 (TR1 elevation) - no truss details; S00.03 S9
Question

TR1 is 27.4 m long and must ship in 3 pieces. No splice, apex or bearing details are shown.

Splice weld: S9 asks for 8 mm fillet welds on 16 plate, but the chord and diagonal walls at the splice are only 6 and 4 mm.

For the builder / transport: the three TR1 pieces are 3336, 2911 and 3601 high (truss depth), so they travel as over-size loads.

Proposal A (our model)
Splices at X 9198 and X 20188 (pieces 9162 / 10958 / 7250). Chords: PL16 end plates 270x190, 4-M20 8.8/S, 6 CFW all round (weld limited by the 6 / 4 mm tube walls). Diagonals crossing the splice line cut on the same line with PL16 270x140 end plates, 4-M20. Apex: top chords mitred, apex vertical welded to both chords (6 CFW all round); no extra bearing stiffeners.
Proposal B
Engineer to issue the splice and apex details, including the splice weld size.
Please confirm A or B. Builder: please note the piece heights for transport.

Awnings

Awning beams to wall panels: moment or cleat

LocationWest entry awning (grid A, 2 SB5); east awning (2 SB1 310UB); G/01 awning (2 SB5, 1.8 m cantilevers)
Drawing ref.S04.13 Detail 7A Typical Moment End Plate at Awning; S04.12 Beam to Column Cast-in Plate Detail; S03.01 Mezzanine Floor Framing Plan

(a) West entry awning and east awning: detail 7A

Question

Detail 7A shows a moment end plate at the awning (16 end plate, 10 gusset, 4M20 ferrules, rows 200 apart). It is drawn once, at grid A. Our model uses detail 7A on the west entry awning (2 SB5, 250PFC) and on the east awning (2 SB1, 310UB). Please confirm detail 7A for these four beams.

Other points here: the east awning edge beam north end lands on the grid G panel end face (170 thick); its south-east corner joint has no detail. The east awning RA on the grid 05 wall is 212 lower to carry the purlins.

Proposal A (alternative)
Simple cleat: cast-in plate PL16 (by panel supplier) + PL12 cleat, 3-M20 8.8/S; cleat site welded 6 CFW to the cast-in plate. Edge beam north end: cast-in plate 120x320.
Proposal B (our model)
Detail 7A: PL16 end plate with PL10 gusset, 4-M20 8.8/S into cast-in ferrules, rows 200 apart (west entry awning and east awning beams).

(b) G/01 awning: both beams on cast-in plate + cleat

Question

The G/01 awning has two SB5 (250PFC) beams, each a 1.8 m cantilever from the grid G wall. The north beam lands on the 170 wide end of the grid 01 panel. Detail 7A does not fit there: the 4 ferrules would be 2 and 8 from the panel faces (ferrules need at least 100 from panel edges and joints, and the 110 deep ferrule hole has no panel around it).

So our model keeps the two G/01 beams the same: a cast-in plate with a cleat, which is a simple connection. Do the two 1.8 m cantilevers work with this connection? If not, please give another fixing or support.

Proposal A (our model)
Both G/01 beams: cast-in plate PL16 (north beam 130x250 in the panel end, 10 and 30 from the panel faces; south beam 150x250 in the grid G panel face), PL12 cleat with 3-M20 8.8/S to the PFC web, cleat site welded 6 CFW to the cast-in plate. Engineer to confirm the cantilevers work, or give a back-span or other support.
Proposal B
Detail 7A on both G/01 beams. For the north beam either (B1) the panel supplier casts a plate or ferrules into the panel end, designed for the cantilever moment, or (B2) the north beam moves about 270 south so its ferrules sit in the grid G panel, 100 clear of the joint; the G/01 awning then becomes about 1530 wide instead of 1800 (architect to accept).

(c) Detail 7A on the deeper beams, and the roof sheeting

Question

Detail 7A is drawn for a 150 deep beam. On the 250PFC and the 310UB we keep the rows where 7A puts them from the beam top (125 above, 75 below), so on the 310UB the lower row is 229 above the underside. Are 4-M20 8.8/S with rows 200 apart enough for the 3.8 m long 310UB cantilevers of the east awning?

The gusset stands 165 above the beam top, so it comes up through the awning roof sheeting at the wall. The sheeting needs a cut-out and a flashing around each gusset.

Proposal A (our model)
Detail 7A as drawn on all four beams: 4-M20 8.8/S, rows 200 apart, gusset 165 above the beam top; sheeting cut and flashed around the gussets by others.
Proposal B
You give more or larger bolts or a deeper end plate for the 310UB, and/or a gusset that stays below the sheeting.
Please answer (a) B or A; (b) A or B (B1 or B2); (c) A or B.
Reply:
